You are in for a treat if you start watching Dota 2 now. The International is going to be incredible this year. The game itself is in a very stable position where many strats are viable. Roughly 8% of heroes have been picked in the group stage (last I heard 26 were unpicked) which is very high in terms of utility.

On top of that the teams are phenomenally strong with many surprising wins during the group stage.

Unfortunately for Dota 2 (warning: opinion incoming) it's hard to get behind an entire team since they change players a lot. Valve is hoping to change that with its new tournament layout utilizing 4 majors each year with limited player changes allowed. It will be interesting to see full details (I don't think they're been released yet?)

For me and Dota 2 I enjoy watching specific players. Dendi (Na'Vi) is a legend, imo, and a real character outside of matches. Fantastic personality and funny to see him troll interviewers. Look up some interviews with him on YouTube, or even better watch the Valve documentary about E-Sports.

Other players I love to watch:

BigDaddy (formerly known as n0tail) is at the top of his game. He has legitimised bootless IO (Wisp - the ball of light) as a legitimate build in pro matches, but it should not be repeated in pubs! He gained many fans when he played for Fnatic and is possibly the best (pro) Meepo player around. Unfortunately it's been a while since I saw him play Meepo but he does it so well. He currently plays support for Cloud 9 and does a real standout job of it.

Iceiceice (Vici Gaming) is another favorite of mine. His individual skill and finesse is awe inspiring and can pull off some amazing shit.

You can watch Ti5 matches in the Dota 2 client for free, both live and as replays, though the best way to watch is via Twitch.tv. The production value of the Twitch casts is amazing these days and have improved in leaps and bounds from 2-3 years ago. The personalities mingle well and I don't think I've seen any of them clash. You'll soon find your favorite caster and fall in love with their quirks. Many of them have incredible technical knowledge of the game and an insane ability to see and call things during even the most intense team fights.

CS:GO. I love watching CS. It's a bit more fast paced then Dota 2 in that rounds are short and usually when shit goes down it goes down fast. The reaction speed and pixel perfect accuracy of the players is incredible. I find it easier to like a whole team in CS since the scene is slightly more stable in terms of player changes.

For me, pashabiceps is a player I enjoy watching. His personal stream is entertaining and he does some amazing work in tournaments. He's got an incredibly likeable personality and interacts with his fans on twitch fairly regularly. He's got to be the most human of all professionals that stream and you can see his genuine love for fans in some of his videos where he receives large donations. My favorite was when he received a $15k donation and thanked the donator profusely, leaving his game to get his daughter and thanking him for his generosity.

In a scene that doesn't have the high stakes like Dota does it takes a lot to stay at the top of your game. I don't know the details behind income in the CS:GO scene but when you compare its prize pools to that of Dota 2 they are not huge.
I just go to csgolounge.com and watch the streams from there for CS:GO tournaments/matches. Since they use a lot of streaming sites other than Twitch I find it easier.
